entry_points.summary: Propagates approved changes through plan artifacts; Phase 9 elevation proposer via propose-prefs.py after finalize.

Read-only multi-dimension audits; Phase 0 scope probe (LIGHT/MEDIUM/HEAVY) with single-file fast-path; --scope-from for HEAVY sub-flow fan-out. Active-plan registry lifecycle: register after slug derivation, seed scope, overlap scan, deregister on completion or abort (FINALIZE_STATUS rule).
Audits existing SPEC/PLAN/TASKS; Phase 5 resolver pre-check (workflow.audit_to_amend); check-no-ask halt branch emitting audit_halt; Phase 9 elevation proposer.

Audits plan artifacts for code-quality issues before implementation; requires STYLE.md (hard gate); Phase 5 resolver pre-check; check-no-ask halt branch emitting plan_style_halt; Phase 9 elevation proposer; emits PLAN_STYLE_AUDIT.md.

Seeds planning with parallel ideation and anti-bias checks. Phase 0 scope probe (LIGHT/MEDIUM/HEAVY) with single-file fast-path (scope_probe_skipped_fast_path); per_vendor/per_framing axis taxonomy. HEAVY Phase 4 presents a (chunk x framing) selection matrix.

Runs heavy hypothesis-tournament debugging with post-mortem and Phase 10 memory review (shipped branch only); sequential AskUser loop capped at 3 candidates; emits memory_review_terminal. Active-plan registry lifecycle: registers in Setup, deregisters on all exit paths (FINALIZE_STATUS rule). When experiment.persona_rotation=true, Phases 3a/3b/7 use fixed 5-panel (agy, cursor@claude-4.6-sonnet, cursor@grok-4.3, cursor@composer-2.5, codex-cli) instead of 2-consultant path; each arm logs persona_bound with selection_source=fixed_panel.

Executes tiny plan-free changes with review gates. Calls config.py export-env during Setup; guards notifications via should-notify wrappers. Doc-fetcher dispatch gated on Z_HARNESS_DOCS_ALWAYS_APPLY (skipped when=never, Phase 2). Active-plan registry lifecycle: registers after do_run_start, seeds scope, runs overlap scan, deregisters on completion or abort (FINALIZE_STATUS rule).
Exports commands/agents/skills to Cursor, Codex, or agy via adapter scripts; defaults to all targets.
Ships diagnosed bug fixes with consult and Codex review; slug-confirm resolver gate (workflow.slug_confirm) after hard collision check; check-no-ask halt branch emitting fix_halt.
Transitions a follow-up entry from verify to done via human approval (--via=human) or 11-point audit evidence validation (--via=audit --evidence=<path>). Nest-guarded.
Transitions any-state follow-up entry to dismissed (terminal). Requires --reason. Nest-guarded.
Read-only merged view of project+global follow-up sinks, priority-sorted. Filters: --status=, --sink=, --priority=. --json for machine consumers. Nest-guarded. Never rebuilds views.
Interactive follow-up consumer: priority-sorted (P0 first), worktree check, staleness check, claim under lock, execute recommended_command, status writeback, auto-close attempt. Nest-guarded.
Re-stamps capture_head and file_blob_hashes for a blocked (staleness) entry, transitions back to open. Only valid for staleness-blocked entries. Nest-guarded.
Diagnostic: counts per status, per-entry and global lock state (flock-probed), oldest open entry, last Notion sync failure. Read-only. Never rebuilds views. Nest-guarded.

Orchestrates task queues with fresh subagents, reviewers, and auto memory review (Phase 9). Phase 0.0 active-plan registry: registers after structural validation (after Setup steps 1-2b-3), seeds scope via scope-extractor, runs graduated overlap scan (OVL_RC 0/10/20/other), sends heartbeats, deregisters via FINALIZE_STATUS rule. Phase 0.1 consumer check: halts with implement_halted_followup_running if project sink has status=running entries (dict-safe parse). N=2 cross-cluster parallel dispatch when overlap_count==0; cycle-2 skip-on-clean-cycle-1; check-no-ask halt branch on second review failure emitting task_halt+implement_end (workflow.implement_all_proceed); Phase 9 emits memory_review_complete — no in-phase AskUser loop. Step 5.0 persona-rotation block (gated on experiment.persona_rotation): random-for-role implementer draw (or forced-control on Nth cadence), persona-draw.json state, PERSONA_PREFIX prepended to prompt, dual reviewer (base_codex + random_arm advisory). Emits persona_attempt_outcome at attempt close. Step 6 reviewer gate and Step 7a retry reviewer gate are consult-aware: when resolve-provider.py reviewer returns none (Z_HARNESS_CONSULT=off), skips external codex-reviewer and dispatches self-reviewer subagent (agents/self-reviewer.md, read-only, Opus), emitting no_consult_dispatch + self_review_completed per task-cycle; consult=on path unchanged.

Implements one pending task with model selection and review. Phase 0.0 active-plan registry (ordering: 0.2 slug discovery -> 0.0 register -> 0.1 consumer check): registers, seeds scope, runs overlap scan, deregisters via FINALIZE_STATUS rule. Phase 0.1 consumer check: halts with implement_halted_followup_running if project sink has status=running entries (dict-safe parse). Phase 2 persona-rotation block mirrors z-implement-all step 5.0 (gated on experiment.persona_rotation): single attempt_id=<task-id>-v1, random-for-role implementer or forced-control, dual reviewer dispatch.
Retrospects one run and proposes harness improvements.
Bootstraps two-tier human and LLM documentation.
Refreshes stale docs and previews proposed updates.
Reviews branch diffs into ranked task-shaped findings; requires STYLE.md.

Unattended pipeline orchestrator. Chains sub-commands via Z_HARNESS_NO_ASK=halt. Presets: full-build, research-build, quick-build. Supports resume <RUN_ID>. Writes MORNING_REPORT.md via morning-report.py; push-notifies on completion/halt. Lock: $BASE/.overnight.lock (flock-guarded). State: overnight-state.json. v1 limit: 12 registered halt-from-ask callsites.
Plans and ships small focused changes via FIX.md.

Splits large work into one-level cluster plans. Active-plan registry lifecycle: registers in Setup, seeds scope, runs overlap scan, deregisters on completion or abort (FINALIZE_STATUS rule). Uses all_plan_slugs for collision detection.

Produces SPEC.md, PLAN.md, TASKS.md. Calls config.py export-env during Setup. Active-plan registry lifecycle: registers immediately after run_start, seeds scope via scope-extractor subagent (Phase 8), sends heartbeat at Phase 8 boundary, deregisters via FINALIZE_STATUS rule. Slug discovery uses all_plan_slugs; slug-confirm resolver gate (workflow.slug_confirm) after hard collision check; check-no-ask halt branches at workflow.slug_confirm and workflow.plan_decisions_approval (both emit plan_halt). Step 9c consolidated freshness gate emits precontext_freshness_acknowledged; proceed-with-stale and abandon set to_command: null in plan_route_decision. Phase 3 and Phase 7 honor Z_HARNESS_CONSULT=off: when resolve-provider.py consultant_primary returns none, all consultant Agent() calls are skipped, tentative decisions recorded as final, consult_skipped event emitted (phase:3 or phase:7). When experiment.persona_rotation=true, Phases 3 and 7 use fixed 5-panel (agy, cursor@claude-4.6-sonnet, cursor@grok-4.3, cursor@composer-2.5, codex-cli) instead of 2-consultant path; selection_source=fixed_panel.
Probes PATH for LLM CLIs and writes providers.json with interactively-confirmed role bindings.
Maps terrain with citations and cross-LLM critique. No recommendations — terrain only. Produces MAP.md. See /z-research for synthesis across map + brainstorm.

Higher-order meta-orchestrator: composes /z-map and /z-brainstorm (parallel when both run), then runs adversarial synthesis panel (3 perspectives + research-judge) producing RESEARCH.md with 10-section schema. Phase 1 parallel dispatch uses first-event kind field (map_run_start/brainstorm_run_start) to identify sub-run archives. Cost 3-6M tokens; AskUser cost gate at invocation.

Final-gate reviews cumulative implementation, then auto-runs memory review (Phase 7). Phase 0 consumer check: halts with review_halted_followup_running if project sink has status=running entries (dict-safe parse). Phase 3.7.5 routes non-halting (major/minor) findings to project sink via scripts/sink-add.sh + parse-followups-block.py; emits followups_routed_to_sink. check-no-ask halt branch at workflow.review_all_proceed emits review_halt and writes partial .review_state.json (halted: true, halt_reason: no_ask_blocked); re-invocation detects this and resumes at Phase 3.7 via review_resume_from_halt event.
Diagnoses and patches misleading skill or command files.

Reports run progress, timing, cost, next step, and memory-review activity (Phase 4b). Phase 0b unconditionally prints resolved base, repo-id, and active-plan count from the active-plan registry as a header before slug-specific output.
Authors STYLE.md from idiomatic captures + cross-LLM critique; --amend mines dismissal clusters.

Delegates memory authoring; accepts --from-candidate-json for automated candidate ingestion; accepts --kind routing-preference (with --question-id, --value, --strength, --scope, --reason) for structured workflow preference writes to docs/llm/workflow.json or docs/llm/workflow-<project-slug>.json.
Drafts semantic TESTS.md cases and links them to tasks.
Updates the z-harness plugin to the latest version.

Tiered bulk codebase quality uplift: decompose repo, cross-cut pass, per-component audits, sequential implement. Slug-confirm resolver gate (workflow.slug_confirm) after hard collision check; check-no-ask halt branch emitting uplift_halt.

Read-only concurrent-run diagnostic. No LLM calls, no subagent dispatch, no writes, no telemetry events. Phase 0: prints resolved base + repo-id from plan-path.sh. Phase 1: lists all active plans from active-plan-registry.py (slug, command, phase, branch, current_task, age, status); stale if last_heartbeat >30 min. Phase 2: optional path-overlap query via --run-id <id> or Z_HARNESS_RUN_ID (OVL exit 0=none, 10=advisory, 20=blocking). Robust to registry unavailability — always exits cleanly.

invariants: Commands are Markdown procedure specs; planning, research, audit, and test commands do not write production code unless explicitly scoped to do so.
Route checks collect deterministic signals first; planning-router is advisory only when deterministic signals conflict.
Every route decision writes route-decision.md, emits plan_route_decision, asks the user, and never auto-executes the target command.
Primary routes are z-do, z-plan-light, z-plan, z-plan-split, z-brainstorm, and z-research; contextual exits include z-audit-plan, z-fix, z-debug, z-amend, and z-maintain-docs.
z-audit-plan is valid only with existing plan artifacts and remains read-only.
Review-family commands preserve evidence separately and promote only actionable findings into task-shaped artifacts consumed by z-implement-all --tasks.
z-implement-all preserves fresh-context implementation by delegating tasks to implementer and reviewer subagents.

[registry] Run-creating commands (z-plan, z-implement-all, z-implement-next, z-do, z-debug, z-audit, z-plan-split) register with active-plan-registry.py immediately after slug discovery and structural validation. Overlap is advisory (lockless safe); strict mode (Z_HARNESS_STRICT_OVERLAP=1) adds one hard gate on explicit x explicit exact path collision.

[registry] FINALIZE_STATUS rule (single source of truth per run): after REG_RC==0, any run-ending halt sets FINALIZE_STATUS=aborted and calls deregister --status aborted before exiting. Normal completion deregisters with complete. If register failed (REG_RC==3 or other nonzero), never call deregister — no record exists.

[registry] REG_RC==3 means register FAILED (no record written). Orchestrator logs registry_error, then: interactive -> AskUserQuestion proceed/abort; unattended -> proceed+log (or halt if Z_HARNESS_STRICT_OVERLAP=1). Do NOT deregister on abort (no record). Any other nonzero REG_RC is treated identically to REG_RC==3.

[registry] OVL_RC==0 (no overlap) proceed silently. OVL_RC==10 (advisory) present AskUserQuestion: proceed/wait/abort; under Z_HARNESS_NO_ASK proceed+log. OVL_RC==20 (blocking, strict mode only, explicit x explicit) hard halt. Any other nonzero log registry_error and proceed (inconclusive degrades to uncoordinated, never halts).

[registry] Scope seed via scope-extractor subagent is best-effort non-fatal: update-scope returns 0 by design and self-logs registry_error on internal failure. Orchestrator calls it with || true and does NOT add a redundant log.
[registry] z-plan heartbeat fires at Phase 8 boundary (best-effort, non-fatal, || true). z-implement-all heartbeats fire at equivalent implementation phase boundaries.
[registry] z-where is purely read-only: no events, no writes, no LLM calls, no subagent dispatch. Always exits cleanly even when registry is unavailable.

[registry] z-stats Phase 0b reads active-plan count unconditionally (NOT gated behind Z_HARNESS_EXPLAIN_RESOLUTION or any env var). Fallback on registry failure: print 'Active plans: (registry unavailable)' and continue.

[rotation] When experiment.persona_rotation=true, z-implement-all and z-implement-next each draw one implementer persona per attempt via random-for-role (or forced-control on cadence); dual reviewer (base_codex + random_arm advisory); ONE persona_attempt_outcome per attempt at close.

[rotation] When experiment.persona_rotation=false, all rotation behavior is a complete no-op — no draw events, no state files, no PERSONA_PREFIX, no outcome events, identical behavior to pre-experiment.
[rotation] z-plan and z-debug use fixed 5-panel (selection_source=fixed_panel) when experiment.persona_rotation=true; no random draw for consultant phases.
[rotation] persona_attempt_outcome status field uses 'done' (not 'ok') — aligns with implement_end status values.
[rotation] Random-arm reviewer verdict is advisory only — it must NOT change halt/retry behavior. Only base_codex reviewer determines review outcome.
Long consult-heavy phases use explicit compaction breakpoints or resumable state files where specified.

z-implement-all Phase 9 and z-review-all Phase 7 are soft auto-memory-review phases: all failure paths (malformed output, skipped helper, empty candidates) exit silently without halting the parent command.
z-debug Phase 10 is also a soft auto-memory-review phase and follows the same contract; the abandoned branch does not invoke run-memory-review.sh.

z-implement-all Phase 9 emits memory_review_complete (not memory_review_terminal) when N>=1 candidates are persisted to JSONL; there is no sequential AskUserQuestion loop in Phase 9. z-review-all Phase 7 follows the same pattern.

z-debug Phase 10 memory review requires exactly one memory_review_terminal event per invocation: the helper emits it on all skip paths; the orchestrator emits it after the user-gate loop for ran_empty and needs_user paths. Phase 10 presents candidates sequentially (capped at 3 per run) via AskUserQuestion.
z-debug Phase 10 uses a 5-line stdout contract with run-memory-review.sh: line 1=status, line 2=cumulative_diff_path, line 3=spec_path (may be empty), line 4=tags_path, line 5=debug_md_path.

Memory candidates surfaced by Phase 9/Phase 7 are persisted to JSONL and surfaced to the user via push-notify pointing to z-suggest-memory --from-candidate-json; they are not presented in-phase. Phase 10 candidates are presented in-phase sequentially.
z-uplift never writes production code directly; it orchestrates audits via auditor subagents and delegates implementation to z-implement-all.
z-uplift gates on STYLE.md presence and doc-staleness before decomposition; it never auto-invokes z-style-init or z-maintain-docs.
z-uplift MANIFEST.md is the single source of truth for component state across phases and resumes; all state transitions are atomic via tmp-then-rename writes.
The cross-cutting synthetic component is excluded from Phase 3 per-component audit iteration and is handled in Phase 5 only.
perf is excluded from z-uplift default dimensions to bound cost; must be added explicitly via --dimensions.
z-style-init Mode A refuses if STYLE.md already exists; Mode B refuses if STYLE.md does not exist.
z-style-init grounds rules in observed source files and interview answers; it never invents rules that contradict observed code.
z-export delegates all file I/O to adapter scripts; the command itself performs no writes.
z-providers-discover enforces consultant_primary != consultant_secondary before writing providers.json.
z-providers-discover writes atomically via tmpfile+rename; it never leaves a partial providers.json.
z-audit-plan-style requires STYLE.md at repo root; there is no --no-style escape. Absence causes immediate refusal and routing to z-style-init.
z-audit-plan-style is read-only; plan mutations happen only via /z-amend applied to surviving PLAN_STYLE_AUDIT.md findings.
z-audit Phase 0 (scope-probe) is skipped when --scope-from is present; SKIP_PHASE_0=true is set before slug derivation, doc-fetcher, or run_start logging.

z-audit Phase 0 also has a single-file fast-path: when the target argument is a single file path with no whitespace, scope-probe is skipped and the target is auto-classified as LIGHT; emits scope_probe_skipped_fast_path.
z-brainstorm Phase 0 also has a single-file fast-path identical in structure to z-audit's; emits scope_probe_skipped_fast_path with command=z-brainstorm.

z-audit --scope-from always uses absolute-path-with-fragment form when dispatched by HEAVY fan-out; bare chunk IDs are for manual invocation only and require PARENT_RUN_ID + PARENT_SLUG in caller context.
z-brainstorm Phase 0 uses axis taxonomy [per_vendor, per_framing]; low-confidence probe results downgrade to MEDIUM without AskUser in v1a.
z-brainstorm sub-flows (HEAVY fan-out) skip Phase 0 entirely — anti-sprawl invariant prevents recursive fan-out.
z-brainstorm HEAVY Phase 4 presents a (chunk x framing) selection matrix; N_PAIRS <= 12 uses a single AskUserQuestion, N_PAIRS > 12 uses two-step chunk-then-framing selection.
z-brainstorm HEAVY abandons set chosen_framing: abandoned (not chosen_pair) to keep abandon detection uniform across LIGHT/MEDIUM/HEAVY modes.
All commands that fire notifications call scripts/config.py should-notify --event <type> and act only when the return is yes; no command checks Z_HARNESS_NOTIFY_LEVEL directly.
Commands that send notifications or apply docs call scripts/config.py export-env during Setup before any phase runs; z-do and z-plan are the canonical examples.
Resolver hooks (resolve-question) branch on {result: skip|prefill|ask}; a resolver error (any non-zero exit) always falls back to asking the user normally — never silently skips.

The hard slug-collision check (PLAN.md/TASKS.md already in slug dir) runs unconditionally in z-plan, z-fix, and z-uplift before resolve-question is called; the resolver only governs the soft non-obvious-slug gate that follows.

z-audit-plan Phase 9, z-audit-plan-style Phase 9, and z-amend Phase 9 are soft elevation-proposer phases: if propose-prefs.py returns empty or a non-zero exit, the phase is skipped silently with no AskUserQuestion surfaced.

z-suggest-memory --kind routing-preference writes to docs/llm/workflow.json (global) or docs/llm/workflow-<project-slug>.json (project); the file is created with INDEX.json registration if absent; MEMORIES-FLAT.md is regenerated after every write.
Suppression entries in .z-harness/.propose-suppress are keyed by question_id with a Unix-epoch expiry (30 days); an unexpired entry causes the elevation proposer to skip entirely.

z-plan step 9c is the sole consolidated freshness gate covering docs-staleness, research-staleness, and map-staleness in one AskUserQuestion. Proceed-with-all-stale emits precontext_freshness_acknowledged (sources list = research/map as applicable) and sets to_command: null in plan_route_decision. Abandon also sets to_command: null.

z-research Phase 1 dispatches /z-map and /z-brainstorm in a single parallel message when DISPATCH_MAP=ran AND DISPATCH_BRAINSTORM=ran. Sub-run archive identification uses the first event's kind field (map_run_start vs brainstorm_run_start) in each archive's events.jsonl — not the directory name. If identification fails, the orchestrator aborts with a run_end error rather than guessing.

z-implement-all N=2 cross-cluster parallel dispatch fires only when overlap_count==0 in SHARED-CONCERNS.md frontmatter; emits cross_cluster_parallel event before dispatching the pair. Plans with overlap_count!=0 always run serially. N=3 parallel cross-cluster dispatch is v2.

z-implement-all cycle-2 skip-on-clean-cycle-1 fires when CYCLE==2 AND cycle-1 reviewer returned blockers=0 AND majors=0, regardless of the reason the implementer re-ran. Emits review_skipped_clean_cycle1 before skipping to step 7b.

check-no-ask is fail-closed: it returns halt|proceed and correctly handles Z_HARNESS_ASK_ALL=1 vs Z_HARNESS_NO_ASK=halt conflicts (exit 5). A resolver error (non-zero from resolve-question) does NOT cause halt — it falls back to asking. check-no-ask exit 5 is a hard config-conflict error, distinct from resolver error paths.

Seven commands are instrumented with check-no-ask halt branches: z-plan (workflow.slug_confirm → plan_halt; workflow.plan_decisions_approval → plan_halt), z-fix (workflow.slug_confirm → fix_halt), z-uplift (workflow.slug_confirm → uplift_halt), z-audit-plan (workflow.audit_to_amend → audit_halt), z-audit-plan-style (workflow.audit_to_amend → plan_style_halt), z-review-all (workflow.review_all_proceed → review_halt + .review_state.json), z-implement-all (workflow.implement_all_proceed → task_halt + implement_end on second review failure).

z-overnight sets Z_HARNESS_NO_ASK=halt ONLY around each Skill call; the parent orchestrator's own AskUserQuestion prompts run with NO_ASK unset. Hard halts (slug collision from overnight-preflight.sh, lock corruption, state corruption, empty chain) are never bypassed by the allowlist or halt-from-ask.
z-overnight overnight-state.json writes are always flock-guarded on $BASE/.overnight.lock using tmp+rename. Lock is released in Phase 4.5 even if MORNING_REPORT.md write fails.
z-overnight sub-run archive identification uses a directory snapshot diff of $BASE/archive/ (excluding *-overnight-* dirs); NEW_COUNT=0 or NEW_COUNT>1 → error + run_id_ambiguous event.
z-overnight resume HEAD SHA validation emits head_sha_mismatch_at_resume warning and proceeds anyway — it does not halt.

z-review-all halted-state resume: if .review_state.json has halted: true AND halt_reason: no_ask_blocked, emit review_resume_from_halt and jump to Phase 3.7 re-run; do NOT delete the state file. Phase 3.7 re-runs check-no-ask from scratch.
z-plan workflow.plan_decisions_approval halt branch emits plan_halt with question_id: workflow.plan_decisions_approval; a subsequent /z-plan resume re-enters at Phase 2.5.

Phase 0 consumer check in z-implement-all, z-implement-next, and z-review-all reads index.view.json as a dict with entries as an object (not a list); uses entries_obj.values() for iteration. A missing or malformed index.view.json yields RUNNING_COUNT=0 — never causes a false halt.
z-implement-all and z-implement-next emit implement_halted_followup_running on consumer-check halt; z-review-all emits review_halted_followup_running (distinct event kind).

z-review-all Phase 3.7.5 sink writes are best-effort: per-entry errors are logged and skipped; the step never blocks the review pipeline. If scripts/sink-add.sh is absent, the step is silently skipped.

All six z-followup-* commands carry a nest guard (Z_HARNESS_FOLLOWUP_CALLER_DEPTH >= 1) that fires before any other logic; nested invocations from within a running follow-up entry's recommended command always fail immediately.
z-followup-list and z-followup-status are read-only and never trigger view rebuilds or acquire locks.
z-followup-next is the only followup command that acquires per-entry locks; it checks the global cross-tool lock ($HOME/.z-harness/.followup-vs-implement.lock) before claiming.
z-followup-refresh is only valid for blocked entries whose block reason is staleness; other block reasons are rejected with an explicit error.

z-plan Phases 3 and 7 honor Z_HARNESS_CONSULT=off: when resolve-provider.py consultant_primary returns the none sentinel, all consultant Agent() calls are skipped in that phase, tentative decisions are recorded as final in phase3-decisions-final.md, and a consult_skipped event is emitted with {phase:3} or {phase:7}. The consult=on code path is entirely unchanged.

z-implement-all Step 6 (reviewer gate) and Step 7a (retry reviewer gate) are both consult-aware: when resolve-provider.py reviewer returns none (Z_HARNESS_CONSULT=off), the external codex-reviewer is replaced by a self-reviewer subagent (agents/self-reviewer.md) dispatch. The self-reviewer is read-only (no Edit/Write tools) and uses the same response shape as the standard reviewer; Step 7 branching (blockers/majors counts) is therefore identical for both paths.
no_consult_dispatch is emitted by z-implement-all once per task-cycle when consult=off (not once per run). self_review_completed is emitted immediately after each self-review Agent() call returns.

The none sentinel from resolve-provider.py is the consult=off signal in both z-plan and z-implement-all. Neither command reads Z_HARNESS_CONSULT directly; the provider resolution script handles the mapping.
gotchas: [registry] z-plan Phase 0.0 ordering: register runs AFTER slug discovery (uses all_plan_slugs), collision check, and resolver gate. It must not run before structural validation because a pre-validation register creates a zombie record with no deregister path.

[registry] z-implement-all Phase 0.0 ordering: registration must occur AFTER Setup steps 1 (repo-root check + --tasks fast path), 2 (slug discovery), 2b (tree validation gates), and 3 ($BASE binding). All tree-validation abort paths before Phase 0.0 have no record to deregister.

[registry] z-implement-next Phase 0.0 ordering: 0.2 slug discovery -> 0.0 register -> 0.1 consumer check. This ordering means if Phase 0.1 halts (followup running), a record already exists and must be deregistered (FINALIZE_STATUS=aborted).
[registry] scope-extractor subagent: update-scope returns 0 by design and self-logs registry_error on internal failure. Do NOT add a redundant || log after the call — that would be dead code.
[registry] z-where overlap query exit codes mirror active-plan-registry.py overlaps exit codes (0/10/20/other). z-where renders them as human text but does NOT emit its own telemetry events.

[rotation] persona_attempt_outcome is emitted by the orchestrator at attempt close, not by the implementer subagent. Passes/pauses (needs_clarification, decision_needed, spec_problem) are NOT attempt closes — they resume the same attempt with the same persona.

[rotation] On retry, the draw is excluded from the previous persona via --exclude so the retry gets a different persona. This is per-spec; the prior persona is not guaranteed to be excluded when the pool is large.
[rotation] persona-draw.json check: compare its attempt_id against current attempt_id to detect resume vs retry. File absent = fresh draw; file present with matching attempt_id = resume.
Do not add z-audit-plan as a front-door planning route when no plan exists; route to z-plan instead.
Route chains prevent ping-pong; after two entries or immediate return-to-prior, ask the user to choose.
z-implement-all --tasks derives BASE from the provided tasks file and bypasses normal slug/tree discovery.
Promoted REVIEW-TASKS.md and MR-REVIEW.md artifacts should be pruned by the user before z-implement-all --tasks consumes them.
z-suggest-memory is a thin delegator; memory mutation lives in skills/z-suggest-memory/SKILL.md.
Plain z-maintain-docs is dry-run by default; docs writes require --apply or explicit confirmation.
--from-candidate-json on z-suggest-memory accepts a file path or - (stdin); it is the automated path used by Phase 9/Phase 7/Phase 10 only — interactive callers should omit it.

z-stats Phase 4b reads review_agent_call events from metrics.jsonl; these are emitted by z-implement-all Phase 9, z-review-all Phase 7, and z-debug Phase 10. The section is empty if none of these phases have run yet for the selected slug.

z-implement-all Phase 9 does NOT present a sequential AskUserQuestion loop for candidates — it persists all candidates to JSONL and push-notifies the user to review them via /z-suggest-memory --from-candidate-json. The 3-candidate per-run cap applies only to z-debug Phase 10's in-phase AskUser loop.
z-debug Phase 10 memory review is skipped entirely on the abandoned branch; no memory_review_terminal event is emitted for inconclusive debug sessions.
z-debug Phase 10 clears .notify-dedup-session at the start of each fresh invocation; without this, notify dedup state from a prior session bleeds into the current one.
z-debug Phase 10 D11 push-notify policy: push-notify at most once per (slug, skip_reason) pair for skipped_broken_context states, deduplicated via .notify-dedup-session.

z-debug Phase 2.5 bisect fast-path: all three gates must hold (known-good ref, reproducibility confirmed yes, scriptable repro). Non-ok bisect returns fall through to Phase 3a silently — bisect never blocks the pipeline, never replaces hypothesis generation, and never pre-fills the winning hypothesis.
z-uplift slug collision detection presents one AskUserQuestion per colliding slug before COMPONENTS.md is written; collision resolution choices must be applied before MANIFEST.md initialization.
z-uplift --refresh-component archives both REPORT.md and TASKS.md atomically (stage-then-rename) before resetting the MANIFEST row; both files must exist or the command exits with an error.
z-uplift resume detection reads MANIFEST state before entering any phase; SKIP_TO_PHASE guards must be checked at the top of every skippable phase — not only inside the phase body.
z-uplift cross-cutting context (C-NNN lines) is filtered per component slug using exact-match on the component: field; global or mismatched slugs are silently excluded from the per-component prompt.
z-style-init --amend Mode B exits early (no change) when DISMISSED_SIGNATURES is empty or N_CLUSTERS is 0 after Jaccard clustering with min-2-member filter.
z-style-init --amend add-with-edits interactive free-text flow is deferred to v2; users must reject and manually edit STYLE.md to customize a proposed rule.
z-style-init Phase 4 parallel critique: if both consultants fail, critique is skipped with a log event and the draft proceeds to user review unmodified.
z-style-init --ingest skips the interview and Capture phases entirely; SOURCE is set to 'ingest' in the frontmatter.
z-providers-discover last-assignment-wins for multi-CLI role selections; consultant_primary/consultant_secondary collision triggers a reprompt loop until resolved or one role is unbound.
z-export --target=all runs cursor, codex, agy sequentially — not in parallel. A failed target does not abort subsequent targets.
z-export exits nonzero immediately for unrecognized --target values before running any scripts.

z-audit-plan-style PLAN_STYLE_AUDIT.md is separate from z-audit-plan's PLAN_AUDIT_REPORT.md; correctness concerns from the plan-style-reviewer are noted in a Cross-dimension note but not promoted into amendment blocks.
z-audit-plan-style archives any existing PLAN_STYLE_AUDIT.md before overwriting; this archive is what extract-dismissals.py reads to compute prior dismissal signatures on subsequent runs.
z-audit --scope-from must be parsed BEFORE Setup (before slug derivation, doc-fetcher, or run_start logging); SCOPE_FROM_ERROR is stored for deferred halt after RUN is established.

z-audit HEAVY fan-out chunk-artifact path validation: dest must be under chunks_dir; source absolute paths must start with Z_HARNESS_PLAN_DIR or one of the per-chunk findings_path directories from the sub-flow archive — not arbitrary paths.
z-audit HEAVY reconciliation skips Phase 2 (auditor dispatch) and Phase 3 (merge findings) entirely; those phases produce per-dimension findings files that do not exist in the HEAVY path.
z-brainstorm HEAVY Phase 4 Back-loop is capped at 3 iterations; the fourth Back is treated as Abandon.
z-brainstorm SCOPE-brainstorm.json is the live file read by Phase 4 to determine HEAVY mode; the archive copy is at archive/<RUN>/SCOPE.json. These are different files — do not confuse them.
z-brainstorm scope-probe low-confidence results are silently downgraded to MEDIUM in v1a — no AskUser gate.
Notification policy is now driven by config.py should-notify; do not check Z_HARNESS_NOTIFY_LEVEL directly in command procedures. The canonical reference for knobs is docs/human/config.md.
Resolver pre-check for workflow.audit_to_amend is used in BOTH z-audit-plan (Phase 5) and z-audit-plan-style (Phase 5); the same question_id is shared between the two commands.
The hard slug-collision check runs unconditionally before resolve-question in z-plan, z-fix, and z-uplift; a resolver result of 'skip' does NOT bypass the collision check.
z-suggest-memory --kind routing-preference does not prompt interactively; it writes the memory entry directly. All required flags must be passed at invocation — unlike the default interactive path.
z-plan step 9c to_command: null means the user chose to proceed with stale inputs or abandon — not that a remedy command was selected. /z-stats must not interpret null as a routing failure.

z-research Phase 1 parallel dispatch: when both sub-commands run, two new archive directories appear after the Agent() calls return. The same second-precision RUN-ID timestamp may produce colliding directory names; identification must use the kind field from events.jsonl, not the directory name.

z-implement-all N=2 parallel dispatch uses the global overlap_count from SHARED-CONCERNS.md as a conservative guard; per-pair overlap checking is v2. A plan with overlap_count=1 runs entirely serially even if the specific pair being dispatched has no file overlap.

z-implement-all cycle-2 skip-on-clean-cycle-1 fires regardless of why the implementer re-ran (clarification resolved, decision answered, etc.). The intent is: if cycle-1 found nothing actionable, there is nothing for cycle-2 to find — the guard is not about diff identity.

check-no-ask exit 5 means Z_HARNESS_ASK_ALL=1 and Z_HARNESS_NO_ASK=halt are both set — this is a hard config conflict, not a normal halt. Commands must surface it as an error rather than silently proceeding or silently skipping.

z-overnight v1 known limit: only 12 AskUserQuestion callsites are instrumented for halt-from-ask. Any sub-command callsite outside this set will block the conversation even with Z_HARNESS_NO_ASK=halt. Run scripts/lint-askuser.sh --strict before launching a long overnight chain.
z-overnight resume-after-complete path: if overnight-state.json top-level status==complete, orchestrator presents AskUserQuestion informing the user and exits — it does NOT re-run the chain.
z-overnight AUTODECIDE_EFFECTIVE merge: env var Z_HARNESS_OVERNIGHT_AUTODECIDE (JSON) overrides hardcoded defaults; unknown keys in the env override are silently merged in (not rejected).
z-implement-all check-no-ask halt fires ONLY on second review failure (not first). First failure still re-spawns the implementer normally.

Phase 0 consumer check parses index.view.json as a dict (entries is an object keyed by entry-id, not a list). A list-style parse would silently iterate keys rather than values and always report 0 running entries — the T100 fix uses entries_obj.values().

z-followup-confirm --via=audit requires --evidence=<path>; --via=human is mutually exclusive with --evidence. Mixing the flags or omitting required flags is a hard argument-parse error before any state reads.
z-followup-refresh only accepts entries in blocked state; providing a non-blocked entry ID is an error that exits before acquiring any lock.
z-review-all Phase 3.7.5: sink-add.sh exit code 3 means dedup-skip (entry already exists) — this is not an error. Only non-zero exit codes other than 3 trigger the per-entry warning.

Z_HARNESS_CONSULT=off is detected via resolve-provider.py returning the none sentinel — NOT by reading the env var directly. Commands that check for none: z-plan (consultant_primary, Phases 3+7), z-implement-all (reviewer, Steps 6+7a). A provider config that overrides the env var takes precedence.

consult_skipped (z-plan) and no_consult_dispatch (z-implement-all) are distinct event kinds emitted by different commands. Do not conflate them. consult_skipped carries {phase:3} or {phase:7}; no_consult_dispatch carries {id, reason, reviewer_replaced_by: self_review} per task-cycle.

The self-reviewer in z-implement-all Step 7a (retry path) receives a ROUND v<CYCLE> prompt that focuses on whether prior findings were addressed, identical in structure to the standard codex-reviewer's retry prompt — not a fresh full-diff review.

self-reviewer subagent has no Edit or Write tools by design. If the harness tries to dispatch it as a standard implementer type instead of self-reviewer type, it will behave incorrectly. Always use subagent_type='self-reviewer'.
